By analyzing UMAP representations and applying a one-class SVM classifier, we've been able to achieve a notable improvement in our ability to distinguish normal from anomalous audio, with significant gains of up to 35% over our baseline. Notably, our results suggest that the presence of background noise has a positive impact on performance when applying this method, a finding that could have far-reaching implications for more widespread use.

We examine the behavior of a Fermi gas consisting of SU(N) fermions with a repulsive interaction, and we find that, in a two-dimensional setting at zero temperature, this system exhibits ferromagnetism when the number of fermions is sufficiently small. Specifically, in a gas containing two dimensions, ferromagnetism occurs when the number of fermions is four or greater, and we observe that, in a gas containing two dimensions, the ferromagnetic state becomes stable at any number of fermions when interactions are intensified.

Our research involved using the stacking method to identify pulsars through gamma-ray emission in the energy range of 50 MeV to 100 GeV, utilizing Fermi-LAT data without applying source models. By analyzing 14 months of data, we discovered 16 previously undetected sources, which were later confirmed to be pulsars after examining their light curves. Our study yielded a finding that 16.7% of the point sources were pulsars. We also pinpointed the locations of an X-ray pulsar and a candidate millisecond pulsar, which were not previously detected in gamma rays. Our research revealed that the locations of pulsars and active galactic nuclei in our sample did not differ significantly.

In the fractional quantum Hall effect, magnetic excitations known as magnetorotons are significant. A previous study [Song et al., Phys. Rev. B 72, 245428 (2005)] found a magnetoroton pole in the two-flavor $SU(2)$ system of composite fermions at a fill factor of three, and this work investigates the three-flavor $SU(2)$ system of composite fermions at fill factors of three, four, and five. At a fill factor of four, the system's magnetoroton behaves similarly to that at a fill factor of three, but its energy is doubled. In contrast, at fill factors three and four, the system's magnetoroton loci are distinct from other poles, but at fill factor five, the system's magnetoroton loci overlap with other poles, affecting long-wavelength magneto-roton resonances. A spectral sum rule for magnetorotons was derived and used to calculate the magnetoroton energy and decay length for all fill factors.

The network of Multi-Channel Water-Cherenkov Telescopes, Extreme Energy Events, operates at the Sutherland Observatory in South Africa. 
Composed of 13 telescopes grouped into 4 clusters, EEE employs a unique, advanced telescope design that allows for real-time, three-dimensional analysis of atmospheric data collected over 360 degrees. 
By utilizing this setup, the EEE observatory can perform comprehensive, high-resolution analyses of extensive air showers induced by cosmic rays. 
In this study, the EEE telescope's performance in detecting and analyzing extensive air showers, as well as the system's overall efficiency, will be examined.

The existence of a unique mild solution for the three-dimensional cutoff Boltzmann equation is demonstrated under the condition of small initial data utilizing the Fourier restriction theory by Barron, Eskin and Mourre.

Machine learning models are prone to mistakes when working with imperfect labels.  This can result in overcompensation by trying to fit noisy data.  To address these issues, state-of-the-art methods like Robust-Logit and Balm to the Machine provide a way to train classifiers robust to label noise by combining multiple models.  Our analysis of these methods on both real-world and artificially created datasets shows that they yield better results than a conventional approach.  However, our findings indicate that these advanced methods can be influenced by specific dataset characteristics, which may limit their reliability in evaluating classification performance.  This research also suggests that combining models may be influenced by how they are trained.

In the field extension ${\mathbb F}_{q^n}$, we examine properties of orbit codes, starting with a fundamental finding – orbit codes with a single orbit are characterized by a linear action of a subgroup in the multiplicative group of ${\mathbb F}_{q^n}$. This leads to a broader investigation of subgroups within the multiplicative group and their corresponding actions on orbit codes, focusing on isometries, automorphism groups, and the structure of orbit codes. Furthermore, we demonstrate a novel approach to orbit code construction by introducing a novel orbit code for each subgroup, free of certain code defects, and derive bounds on the minimum distance of this orbit code based on the subgroup's properties.

A precise mass measurement of a star at the turnoff phase in the 4 Gyr-old open cluster M67 was achieved through a precise analysis of Kepler's light curves. The star M67-1 was selected based on its precise parallax from the Gaia EDR3 catalog, its location at the turnoff phase, and its single-epoch spectroscopic classification. By utilizing the Asteroseismic Validation Pipeline for Clusters (AVPI), we were able to determine the star's fundamental parameters, including its mass, radius, and age. The star M67-1 was found to have a mass of 1.32 times the mass of the Sun, a radius of 1.12 times the radius of the Sun, and an age of 1.06 billion years, supporting the theory that the turnoff is the point at which stars become visible.
The system of eigenfunctions for the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c = -d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$ on the semi-axis with specific conditions on the parameter $\alpha$ is found to be complete.

A new, density-based SPH method is introduced that is suitable for simulating a wide range of fluid-based systems in complex environments. The proposed model is enhanced by a novel smoothing approach, incorporating a precise gradient calculation and a modified mass partitioning strategy. These innovations lead to a robust and accurate model, capable of handling diverse interparticle forces and spacings while maintaining reliable performance. Notably, the new method demonstrates robustness and high precision in a range of test cases, achieving accuracy comparable to that of refined mesh-based discretization.

Deep learning-based methods are increasingly popular for recovering hyperspectral images from low-resolution color cameras, yet they're limited by high computational requirements and reliance on large, labeled datasets. A more efficient approach involves using a spectral prior as a small number of discrete spectral bands or a continuous function-based model. However, these methods often fail to account for the unique characteristics of hyperspectral images, including their discrete nature and variability in quality across different pixels. To address this, we propose a Pixel-aware Function-mixture Network that combines the strengths of discrete and continuous spectral prior models. This novel network consists of a feature generator, a module that estimates spectral priors, and a module that fuses the estimated priors with the visual features to produce the final hyperspectral image. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through a series of experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art models and is particularly effective when dealing with small or irregularly shaped hyperspectral image datasets.

In this study, we tackle the issue of assigning geographic tags to objects within street view images. Our approach is unique in utilizing the context provided by street names displayed in the images. To accomplish this, we first leverage a model to identify the text embedded within the images. Subsequently, we construct a model that identifies the geographic location of which street the extracted text refers to. Finally, our model predicts the location within the image where a given object is situated, relative to the street sign for that particular road. Our experiments were conducted using a specially created dataset for this task, and we also developed a new dataset based on the Google Street View dataset. Our approach outperformed a baseline model in accurately predicting the location of objects within the image.

The task of identifying dams and reservoirs from satellite imagery is a complex one due to their small size and frequent overlap. To overcome this challenge, a novel approach known as dam-reservoir extraction from remote sensing images uses a metric learning-based method to classify images as either dams or reservoirs. This method employs a novel metric that minimizes the distance between similar images while maximizing the distance between dissimilar ones. To enhance performance, the system also incorporates a drop-out connection and a feature fusion module. Experiments conducted on the large-scale DamReservoir dataset yielded an impressive 92.61% accuracy, which surpasses the current benchmark by 4.04%. Additionally, the system's effectiveness was demonstrated on a newly assembled dataset of 12 cities in China, which was annotated by experts. The results show that the method can effectively distinguish dams and reservoirs, providing valuable insights for urban planning and environmental research.

This study introduces two key concepts, quasi-finitely separable and QFS-space, examining their fundamental attributes and characteristics, such as distribution, preservation, and symmetry. Additionally, a specific hierarchical structure within the class of LSP spaces is investigated, specifically focusing on QFC and QFS functions.

Predicting the type of a location such as restaurant, shop or museum when its address is unknown can be a useful application with real-world benefits in tasks like finding relevant spots, routing, and dispatching. This paper introduces a new, multi-modal method for predicting a location type based on its textual and visual characteristics extracted from Google Maps. The method leverages a two-pathway transformer model to analyze both text and image features and determine the location type. The proposed approach outperforms existing single-modal methods in predicting location types and also demonstrates the potential of combining multiple modalities to improve accuracy and speed.

Investors rely heavily on the information presented in earnings call transcripts, which provide crucial context missing from financial reports. Researchers are particularly interested in exploring how various factors, such as analysts' questions and management responses, influence stock price fluctuations. To investigate these dynamics, an analysis was conducted on 1,777 transcripts from 2015 to 2017. By examining the relationship between these factors, researchers found that certain queries, like those addressing losses and product launches, are more effective at generating significant stock price movements compared to others. Conversely, certain comments from management failed to have a noticeable impact on stock prices. Interestingly, analysts' queries about acquisitions were met with considerable interest from market investors. Moreover, the analysis revealed that certain words within the transcripts could serve as valuable indicators for potential stock price movements. Ultimately, the goal is to develop a data-driven model that can accurately predict stock price movements based on earnings call transcript content.

We're investigating the issue of covering a complete area with sensor deployments under specific constraints. Initially, we're looking into sensor placements within bounded regions when sensor detection ranges are consistent throughout. Next, we're addressing the scenario where detection ranges vary across different sensors. Notably, achieving an optimal solution for the second scenario remains an unsolved problem within sensor placement literature. In response, we propose a novel algorithm for the initial scenario and adapt it to develop a novel algorithm for the second scenario. Both of these novel algorithms leverage a central concept: sensor placement occurring on a grid. By doing so, we're able to identify the most suitable sensor locations within a predetermined area, thereby minimizing the overall number of sensors required for complete area coverage. Notably, these proposed solutions outperform existing approaches in terms of reduced sensor count and coverage efficiency. Moreover, our algorithms' performance is validated through accompanying software simulations.

A quantum algorithm, eigenstate filtering, extracts low-energy eigenstates from an arbitrary spectral distribution by adapting a quantum phase estimation technique. We prove that, for qubit-based computers, EF's sample complexity - which measures low-energy state amplitude summation over measured values - is minimized by evaluating polynomials related to the energy spectrum. We develop a general EF method incorporating these polynomials and demonstrate its superiority in solving quantum linear systems over established approaches.

We investigate the behavior of compact baby skyrmions that are self-dual, either with or without a gauge field, within a nonlinear medium. By employing the Bogomolny estimate, we establish a criterion for the compactness of these baby skyrmions and examine how a gauge field affects their stability. Additionally, we analyze the impact of the nonlinear medium's index on the compact baby skyrmions' deformations under nonlinear perturbations.

This report summarizes a recent collaboration between theorists and experimenters from CERN to study searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model, focusing on the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). The collaboration's work was motivated by the significant advancements in the LHC's luminosity and the potential of future colliders, and included a workshop held at CERN in April 2019. The contributions detailed in this report centered around SMEFT operator searches at current and future colliders, and included input from LHC experiments on interpreting results in the SMEFT framework and potential improvements to collider performance. The collaboration's outcomes were meant to provide guidance for theorists and experimenters working on SMEFT searches and offer suggestions for future directions in collider research.

We have successfully developed and tested a rotating diamond nuclear magnetometer. This device consists of a $7~\mu$m$^2$ diamond flake with $^{13}$C nuclear spins, coupled with a pair of $^{14}$C ions in a Penning trap. The trap's motion caused by rotation can be detected through the interaction with $^{13}$C nuclear spins. Using microwave pulses, the interaction between the spin splittings and the motion-induced magnetic fields was controlled. The device's sensitivity was tested by measuring the interaction with the diamond's electron spins, which were precessing due to an inhomogeneous magnetic field. As a result, the diamond's nuclear spin motion was accurately measured with a root-mean-square error of $0.37\pm 0.09~\mu$m, limited primarily by spin measurement errors.

The development of whole-cell models is driven by the desire to fully understand cellular behavior. Initially, whole-cell models focused on the mechanical properties of individual cells. However, with advancements in technology, researchers can now collect detailed information about cellular functions, allowing for more comprehensive models that incorporate biochemical, biomechanical, and biophysical processes. As digital twins become increasingly relevant for drug development and personalized medicine, there is a growing need for whole-cell models to be used in a wide range of applications. This study provides an overview of the current state of whole-cell modeling, identifies areas for improvement, and outlines key principles for moving forward. Whole-cell models should prioritize simplicity, accuracy, and flexibility, allowing them to be adapted to different cell types and be used in various scenarios. To create and utilize whole-cell models, researchers should adopt a collaborative and open-minded approach, using technology such as 3D printing and artificial intelligence to develop and validate models. Whole-cell models should be accessible to a broad audience and be used to make predictions and support decision-making.

Mobile devices are now equipped with the capability to access and retrieve information from vast databases containing object images. However, existing object image search systems have a limitation in handling real-world scenarios where images are taken from multiple angles. This problem can be addressed by developing an object image search system that can automatically create and store multiple view images of an object and match new images with the best possible views. This research presents a novel mobile system that enables object image search from a variety of perspectives. The system captures and stores multiple view images of an object and matches new images with the best possible views. The system uses a novel image matching approach that considers the object's context and location to guide the search, and employs a hierarchical tree structure to efficiently match the query image with the most similar object. The system also uses a novel feature descriptor that uses a bag-of-words approach to represent the object's context and location. The results show that the proposed system significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in retrieving matching image views, with a 7.2% improvement in mean average precision at 1.0 recall.

A cutting-edge computing technology known as Hyperdimensional (HD) computing, holds promise in improving learning and memory capabilities in systems such as brain machine interfaces and seizure prediction devices.  In this research, we investigated the effectiveness of HD computing in enhancing the performance of a system used for single-channel EEG seizure prediction, while also exploring the impact of varying HD vector count on classification outcomes.  Our findings show that a system using 100 HD vectors and a linear readout outperforms previous approaches by a significant margin, achieving a high classification rate of 94.5% and significantly reducing false alarm rates.  Additionally, we discovered that a system using 100 HD vectors can learn and retain information from as few as 20 examples, making it an attractive choice for real-time seizure prediction, a task that demands rapid learning.

Future observations of gravitational waves from deci-hertz frequency binary black holes can serve as "standard sirens" to determine the Hubble constant with a precision of around 1% and resolve the cosmic tension in Hubble constant measurements with binary black hole events alone. Combining these measurements with those from the future Euclid and JWST satellite observations, we can pinpoint the value of Hubble constant with a precision of around 0.5%. This method also allows for using standard sirens to determine the Hubble constant with a precision of around 1% and is less affected by uncertainties in black hole population models. This makes it a viable solution for resolving the current discrepancy in Hubble constant measurements and a potential area of research for future gravitational wave observations in the deci-hertz frequency band.

We have enhanced the existing question answering dataset QALD-9 by incorporating 403 new queries across 9 languages in order to investigate the translation of questions by native speakers and integrate questions from smaller languages. Our investigation led us to develop a dataset of over 2000 question-answers pairs by translating English questions into French, Spanish, Chinese, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Korean, and Greek. Our methodology also involves collecting and evaluating new questions for German, Finnish, and Czech. Our research provides a more comprehensive framework for evaluating question answering systems across multiple languages and various linguistic groups. The new dataset, known as QALD-9-plus, is publicly available at https://github.com/aksriram/qald-9-plus.

We've developed a groundbreaking approach to fine-tune pre-trained image models, known as the Executive Function (EF) technique, through resampling and relabeling. By leveraging a dataset of pre-trained models, our method generates "hindsight summaries" on test images to inform the learning process. We then adapt a self-supervised technique, using a contrastive loss function, to enable self-learning on test data, effectively eliminating the need for training samples. This direct, fine-tuning approach allows us to skip standard data normalization and augmentation steps, resulting in significant time savings. Our technique yields impressive results, producing state-of-the-art performance on the ADE20K human action recognition task, the ILSVRC 2012 video classification task, and the A2D2 human action recognition task, as well as notable improvements on the Kinetics and Human Action Scene datasets.

The inherent flaws within machine learning algorithms arise from the data used to train them, and we need to understand and address these biases in medical image analysis. We have developed tools to detect biases in medical image datasets using data visualisation methods, and we apply these tools to five publicly available datasets consisting of CT scans, digital retinal photos, magnetic resonance images (MRI), X-ray images and ultrasound images. Our findings show that each dataset is biased in distinct ways, and we propose a method to quantify the extent of this bias. By making biases in data visible, we can create and acquire more comprehensive and fair datasets for medical image analysis.

The impact of noisy data on metric learning systems is significant, particularly in scenarios where training data is inherently noisy due to crowdsourced labeling or when data cleanliness is compromised by mislabeled instances during the initial training phase. Consequently, systems designed to handle noisy data are essential for robust system development. Notably, proxy-based methods have shown promise in this area, by leveraging a clean proxy set to correct metric learning system errors. However, existing proxy-based methods are limited by the rigid assignment of proxies to corresponding classes, which can lead to suboptimal performance when dealing with complex data distributions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel proxy-anchoring scheme, where proxy values align with class centers only when confident, while allowing for the possibility of some data points deviating from this alignment. We develop a proxy-anchoring loss function, which combines a novel instance loss and a class-level proxy loss, ensuring that the proxy loss is zero when the loss minimum is achieved. Through comprehensive experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, particularly in scenarios with severe data noise.

Future large-scale surveys will enable the precise measurement of cosmological parameters by analyzing the large-scale structure of the universe. The traditional analysis of galaxy correlations has been limited by the assumption of a homogenous and isotropic universe, which is not accurately represented by observed data due to sampling and measurement biases. This paper presents an innovative approach to analyze galaxy correlations, which involves modifying the correlation function to enhance its sensitivity to cosmological parameters. The new method is less susceptible to biases and measurement errors, resulting in improved parameter estimates. By applying this method to mock data, significant improvements were observed in the accuracy of cosmological parameter constraints, with a 15% reduction in the uncertainty of cosmological parameters when compared to traditional analyses. The new method was also shown to be more resilient to various sources of bias.

Using a combination of quantum group symmetry and integrability, we develop a method to study a quantum fluid made of atoms that can exhibit SO(5) symmetry, where spin and pseudospin degrees of freedom are coupled in a way that is symmetric under SO(4) transformations and can be further protected by an additional SU(1) symmetry. The resulting phase exhibits features of fractional statistics without the usual occurrence of vortons, instead showing a unique superfluid state with characteristics of instantons moving within the fluid.

Recent advancements in micro-avalanche photodiodes have led to a surge in interest. By introducing a single p-type doping layer, a novel MA type avalanche photodetector has been developed, offering superior characteristics over traditional avalanche photodetectors. Gaining momentum since its inception, the MA technology has seen rapid progress, with focus now on further enhancing its performance through the integration of multiple charge carriers and advanced avalanche geometries. This paper presents a new type of avalanche photodetector featuring MAPD, specifically designed to utilize dual carrier detection and symmetric geometric configurations. By taking advantage of these refined geometries, significant improvements in its operating performance and avalanche mechanisms have been demonstrated.

This study examines how the characteristics of primary ideals in Noetherian local rings, specifically their sectional genera, impact the Cohen-Macaulay property of associated rings, such as Rees rings and Ringel-Fox rings. Notably, we establish that if the sectional genera of finitely many prime ideals equal 0, then the ring is Cohen-Macaulay. This discovery is extended to prime ideals with reduced homology modules. Additionally, we explore connections between the Cohen-Macaulay property and fundamental characteristics of primary ideals, including Gorensteinness, weakly Cohen-Macaulayness, and symmetricity.

A comprehensive investigation of bismuth-based Aurivillius oxides, particularly Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ (BFTO), focuses on its structural and magnetic behavior under the influence of high hydrostatic pressure up to 3.0 GPa. Using nuclear forward scattering, researchers measured the magnetic correlations and domain structures as a function of pressure. Notably, the magnetic phase transitions were observed to shift towards higher pressures. At ambient pressure, the magnetic phase transition occurred between 2.0-2.5 GPa, and then shifted to 2.5-3.0 GPa under pressure. These results indicate that BFTO's magnetic phase is relatively stable under high pressure.

A quantitative analysis is conducted to compare the trading costs generated by standard trading practices, including market orders and limit orders, as offered by major brokerage firms. Although theoretical models are available, empirical research on real trading data and its implications are limited. To address this gap, a novel Bayesian approach called Markov Chain Monte Carlo Probing is developed to efficiently and reliably estimate the trading costs in real-time. This method is applied to the data from four leading brokers to analyze and compare the trading costs in a highly liquid stock, Apple Inc (AAPL). The results demonstrate that a limit order strategy generally generates lower costs than a market order approach, with certain brokers producing higher levels of execution instability than others.

A new optical component called the optomechanical add-drop filter efficiently directs specific wavelengths over a broad range, utilizing a single resonator. In this study, we've developed a fully adjustable OAD-F filter that can target a broad range of wavelengths simultaneously. To achieve this, we've designed a device with three properties: the ability to adjust the filter's wavelength with precision, the capacity to handle a large number of wavelengths, and the capability to control the filter's signal strength. The device's performance surpasses previous designs, boasting a very low level of signal loss. The technology's potential to be easily integrated into a platform using silicon carbide gives us reason to believe that it can be efficiently produced using mass manufacturing techniques.

Public health interventions significantly impact daily life, but evaluating their effectiveness is challenging without access to detailed data on disease transmission and participant numbers. However, the implementation of these interventions creates a digital footprint in digital media that can be used to gauge their effects on the spread of disease. This is feasible because these interventions often alter the content of online publications, altering the likelihood of individuals engaging with specific websites. In this study, we propose an approach for assessing the impact of public health interventions using the content of online publications as a proxy. Our method compares the change in the likelihood of online engagement with particular web pages before and after the implementation of an intervention. We also introduce a statistical test for evaluating the presence of a significant causal link between an intervention and a reduction in online engagement, taking into account potential confounding factors. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through the analysis of an intervention in Catalonia, Spain, aimed at containing the spread of COVID-19, as well as through simulated data.

In modern image compression systems, the use of neural networks to encode images in bits is becoming increasingly popular. Although the focus is often on reducing bit rate, the use of an end-to-end neural network can hinder real-time performance, particularly on limited hardware. To overcome this, we introduce PILC, a fast neural network for lossless image compression, optimized for high-performance GPUs. PILC employs an auto-encoder architecture with an innovative hybrid wavelet-coefficient framework and a learnable hybrid transform, combining the strengths of both wavelet and non-wavelet methods. This framework is paired with a novel conditional entropy model that leverages both probability mass and binning methods to achieve accurate modeling. PILC also includes a fast learning algorithm that utilizes quantization to reduce the computational load during training. Experimental results show that our method surpasses the performance of the latest neural network on the Kodak benchmark, meeting the requirements of real-time applications while maintaining exceptional quality.

Using 4.8 fb^-1 of LHCb data collected at various collision energies, the $B^+$ meson was observed decaying into $D_s^+$ and $K^+K^-$ for the first time. From a fit of the decay amplitude, the branching fraction for this decay was calculated as approximately 7.1 parts per million. The results also ruled out a specific $B^+$ decay into $D_s^+$ and $\phi$ with a confidence level of 95.5%.

Optimal transport distances are widely used in deep learning for measuring distances between probability distributions. However, the presence of outliers poses a significant challenge to existing OT norms, limiting their ability to accurately represent real-world data sets. In response, we introduce a new, robust measure known as Optimal Transport with Outlier Robust Wasserstein (OTORW), which leverages outlier data points to inform the estimation of probability distributions while effectively filtering out the influence of anomalies. By adapting this robustness approach to a broader framework, we establish a connection between OTORW and a modified Kullback-Leibler divergence metric, demonstrating its potential to mitigate the negative consequences of outliers on learning and transport problems.

In this research, we have developed an innovative, team-based approach to address complex strategic planning problems. The primary goal is to design a multi-agent system, comprising AI, Human, and AI-Human collaboration, to tackle high-stakes decision-making challenges. We propose a novel concept of collaborative intelligence, where unique human skills and collective learning between humans and AI agents work in tandem to achieve shared objectives. Our approach involves building AI teammates that mirror human decision patterns, enabling them to effectively partner with humans in problem-solving. By leveraging reinforcement learning and human decision modeling, we have created an adaptable AI teammate capable of collaborating with humans in diverse scenarios. Our results confirm that including humans and AI agents as teammates can significantly enhance team performance compared to teams comprising only humans or solely AI systems.

The natural outcome of supersymmetry in particle physics is that supersymmetric particles should be detectable at the Large Hadron Collider. However, after years of searching, these particles have yet to be found, leading many to question the validity of supersymmetry. This doubt is intensified by the fact that the lightest supersymmetric particles are often predicted to have masses similar to those of regular particles. The mass spectrum of supersymmetric particles is heavily influenced by the properties of supersymmetry-breaking parameters, particularly when they are introduced at a fundamental level. The study of to break supersymmetry leads to an unexpected consequence - a proliferation of supersymmetric states, many of which are light. This work delves into the mechanisms for spontaneous supersymmetry-breaking, focusing on scenarios in which the supersymmetry gauge quantum chromodynamics effect is avoided.

Disciplines and roles vary in communication needs, workloads, and participation, ultimately influencing the design and creation of visualizations. Notably, prior research has revealed differences in spatial abilities among professionals with different roles within the same field. This study examines the relationship between job experience and spatial abilities by comparing performance in completing visualization tasks across disciplines. Our analysis of 1,120 task completions by 280 professionals revealed significant differences in task performance among disciplines. The results suggest that individuals with more professional experience tend to perform better by 7-10%. Additionally, our findings indicate that spatial abilities have a notable impact on task performance and reveal a correlation between the type of discipline and spatial abilities.

We've developed a straightforward concept called clause set cycles that serves as the basis for creating reliable induction rules in automated theorem proving. These rules are capable of accurately handling inductive axioms that have complex effects and no assumption of the Halting Problem. Furthermore, our work includes developing a detailed model for understanding the behavior of a specific type of programming language called while-programs, leveraging a refined version of the clause set cycles concept. This model enables us to create a sound and complete induction rule for a logical system called the while-programs framework, a property that cannot be achieved using traditional induction schemes based on loop formulas.

Graph retrieval is a significant problem in natural language processing that deals with identifying a graph that best matches a query text description. The query text describes a graph consisting of nodes and edges described using natural language. Researchers have made progress in this area, but most of their models rely on neural networks that are trained to solve ranking tasks. This approach can be inefficient and may not provide accurate results due to overfitting and biased training labels. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel method for graph retrieval that uses a neural matching model. We tested our approach using the GraphRet 2020 test dataset, and the results show that it performs better than other top models in the field.

We've found that pre-training neural networks using randomly generated training techniques typically results in stable, well-rounded networks but often struggles with learning complex and unpredictable (or "sequential") patterns. In contrast, conventional approaches like backpropagation tend to work effectively but may not produce such broad and stable networks. In this study, we explore the idea of using similar training methods to help neural networks learn dynamic and non-constant patterns, drawing inspiration from the field of Natural Language Processing. We've developed a novel learning approach called "language modeling for dynamics" and tested it on various types of tasks, such as learning system dynamics, inverse dynamics, trajectory optimization, and control of non-linear systems. Our results show that the proposed method is competitive with traditional backpropagation and can even outperform it in certain cases, especially when dealing with complex and hard-to-predict systems.

In countries where electricity generation falls short of demand, a standard solution is to distribute the available supply across consumers through various methods. This article reviews ten widely used allocation techniques and provides a comprehensive framework to assess their fairness, both in instances of surplus and shortage. The review is accompanied by a novel dataset consisting of a large number of allocation results obtained from 1032 instances of 11 consumers, utilising the web-based Fair-division.org platform. To gauge the fairness of these methods, we employ multiple fairness metrics, which are often defined for fair division scenarios. In our study, we discover that the Fair-division.org platform offers users a favorable experience, as they can easily comprehend outcomes of allocations that slightly favor their interests over others.

A multi-token event comprises a series of occurrences linked in time and space, such as a protest's opening and closing. We define and model this phenomenon as event coreference, a crucial aspect for comprehending news articles and their contents. To address this issue, a two-stage system is proposed to resolve event coreference in areas where annotated data and models are scarce. Experimental results on a new, highly challenging dataset of contentious politics events, which features events with sparse, variable structures, reveal substantial improvements in both precision and recall. Furthermore, our system achieves comparable results to established models in more annotated datasets, and highlights the value of incorporating knowledge-based approaches in scenarios with limited resources.

The Complementarity Knapsack Problem, characterized by real variables, arises in various optimization contexts. It encompasses the Knapsack Problem and Quadratic Programming complementarity issue. This paper focuses on developing new sufficient conditions for generating valid cutting planes for this problem. Specifically, it introduces two new MISO (mixed-integer-set-of-continuous-variables) inequalities that outperform existing MISO of comparable strength. This improvement results in more efficient computation times for these cutting planes. Additionally, the work presents a novel polyhedral transformation technique for the Complementarity Linear Problem, enabling construction of new valid inequalities. A related Complementarity Knapsack Inequality is also explored, defined by restricting non-negativity to a subset of variables. This novel concept facilitates derivation of new valid inequalities through polyhedral transformations.

This paper begins by defining the concepts of generalized $(m,n)$-Jordan derivation, generalized $(m,n)$-Jordan centralizer, and $2$-torsion-free $(m,n)$-Jordan derivation on a ring $R$, before providing examples of such entities. The paper then proves that any $2$-torsion-free linear generalized $(1,n)$-derivation on a semiprime ring $R$ is a centralizer. Additionally, the existence of generalized $(1,n)$-derivations in a semiprime ring $R$ is linked to the presence of a generalized $(1,n)$-derivation of a certain type when $n > 1$. This paper further shows that certain types of generalized $(1,n)$-derivations in a semiprime ring $R$ are centralizers under certain conditions. Finally, the paper establishes that a $2$-torsion-free $(m,n)$-Jordan derivation in a semiprime ring $R$ is a $(m,n)$-derivation when $|m-n|=1$.

We show that Weinberg's well-known two-factor relation arises as a byproduct of
imposing helicity constraints on scattering amplitudes in spin-1 theories. The
constraints derived from the high-energy behavior of scattering amplitudes in two
dimensions reduce the number of independent amplitudes and generate two sets of
relations among them. By applying these constraints, we derive the two-factor
relation, which holds across all momenta and can be used to express any
spin-1 amplitude in terms of a single basic unit. This approach enables us to
find the counterterm that reproduces the two-factor relation at the leading order
when the amplitude is expanded around the on-shell condition.

We demonstrate that in $\mathbb{R}^d$, a family of nonlinear projections with a transversal is equivalent to a sequence of linear projections. This discovery allows us to establish that a sequence of linear maps satisfies a mean contraction property in a metric related to the Favard length if and only if the sequence of nonlinear maps obtained by applying these maps exhibit the same transversality between consecutive measures. Additionally, we define a Favard length metric for families of nonlinear projections and show that it reduces to the Favard length in the case of linear projections. Furthermore, we prove that this metric is invariant under affine transformations and provide a characterization of the maps that contract Favard length uniformly, which leads to the identification of those maps that contract uniformly the modified Favard length, a metric defined in the context of nonlinear projections.

We introduce a framework for efficient guided policy search that involves imitation learning, which enables direct transfer of knowledge from an expert operator. This framework leverages a safety-critical model predictive controller to provide a safe reference policy that guarantees system performance within predetermined limits. Then, an imitation learning agent is trained to replicate this safe reference policy in a risk-averse environment. This agent is designed using a combination of a policy gradient method and a model-based imitation learning approach. The proposed framework is successfully implemented and demonstrated using a 1DOF pendulum, which was controlled remotely by a human-like virtual agent in a first-person simulation.

The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect resulting from an energy-dependent Berry curvature can be represented by a linear Berry curvature.  However, in materials with spin-orbit coupling and certain band structures such as those near topological semicausality, a third-order energy dependence emerges, giving rise to the third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect.  This phenomenon is characterized by a Berry curvature that follows a $E^3$ relationship, and is typically observed at energies greater than the band gap.  This study develops a generalized semiclassical theory capable of capturing this effect, and we apply it to a model system featuring a topological semicausality transition.  Results reveal that third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect is detectable when energy is above the band gap, and its magnitude is influenced by a factor of the square of the Berry curvature at the band edges.  This study provides a theoretical framework for understanding and predicting the third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect, and its implications for future experimental detection of this phenomenon in topological semicausality.

The code's call graph maps which parts of the code trigger or are triggered by one another. Multiple call graphs representing various system executions can form an ensemble, used, for instance, in model checking to guarantee the absence of bugs. These ensembles are crucial in software engineering, especially for large-scale systems with intricate structures. However, visualizing multiple call graphs together can be challenging. Our research presents a new visualization technique called the Call Graph Tracker. This tool displays an adjustable number of call graph paths across multiple visualizations linked together, allowing users to analyze multiple model-checking ensembles efficiently. The researchers conducted user studies to evaluate the effectiveness of the Call Graph Tracker in analyzing large ensembles. The results showed that users could analyze up to 50 call graphs more efficiently with the new tool, and they needed less time to complete a task compared to using traditional call graph visualization methods.

A commonly used benchmark for assessing natural language processing languages like English and German is the 1 Billion Word benchmark, however, the team behind this benchmark has established their own standards for proper language usage based on an idealised, unrealistic representation of human communication. This is evident in their definition of a 'vocabulary curve', which is not supported by empirical evidence from real-world language usage, resulting in several issues, including the dismissal of high-frequency words that are necessary for effective communication and the inclusion of rare words that serve a unique purpose. This paper argues that the 1 Billion Word benchmark's framework is flawed and needs to be reevaluated due to its reliance on unrepresentative vocabulary curve claims and a lack of alignment with the context in which vocabulary is used.

Observations from the Nobeyama Radioheliograph reveal quasi-periodic pulsations (QPP) in radio flux during solar flare events.  Analyzing two events on October 23rd, 2017, which resulted in X6.6 and X1.3 classifications, it was discovered that QPP was present at both flare peaks.  Radio flux oscillations were found to be more pronounced at 91 MHz compared to 1.6 GHz.  To explain these findings, a theoretical model of a magnetic reconnection current sheet was developed, which suggests that QFPs are caused by Alfvén waves propagating along the current sheet.  This supports the theory that QFPs are linked to the propagation of Alfvén waves, which can be confirmed using microwave imaging with high-resolution frequencies.  This method allows for detailed analysis of QFPs and their role in solar flare energy, particularly at the current sheet.

Anomalies can be defined as minor irregularities occurring within nearly ubiquitous processes, making their detection particularly challenging due to their rarity, consistency, and uniformity. The traditional approach to anomaly detection involves segmenting images to uniform areas, applying local features, such as Haralick textures, and using a support vector machine or a random forest to classify images as normal or anomalous. However, this method is often insufficient, as images rarely consist of uniform patterns. Recent advancements in deep learning have been successful in detecting anomalies within images, but often at the expense of computational resources. This research introduces an efficient and straightforward 'a contrario' anomaly detection method that operates at various scales, starting with image blocks and progressively refining its resolution through comparison with smaller windows. The proposed framework is validated through experiments on real-world images obtained from a French automotive manufacturer's quality inspection process.

New well-posedness theorems are established for a class of equations within the KP-I family, originally considered in a previous study by V. Zakharov, that combines dispersion and defocusing-inertial surface dynamics. These results extend the existing literature, particularly a previous fixed-point approach developed by J. B. Taylor, which was initially applied to the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. In this work, multiple variations of the fixed-point formulation are integrated and adapted to the KP-I context. Furthermore, a novel fixed-point formulation is introduced that is more flexible and compatible with a wide range of potential nonlinear terms. This new approach is particularly well-suited to the KP-I equations and enables the achievement of optimal regularity for solutions. By combining this approach with an innovative strategy to manage the dispersive effects, significant gains in terms of the data regularity have been made. In particular, for small initial data, global solutions are proven to exist within the $H^{s}$ space for $s \geq 7/5$, which represents an improvement over earlier results. This research also sheds light on the minimal regularity required for the initial data when employing the original fixed-point formulation.

Kramer's theorem confirms the double degeneracy of a non-degenerate quantum ground state in a time-reversal symmetric and ergodic environment, ensuring identical physical properties under time reversal operations. We discovered, however, that in non-integrable quantum many-body systems coupled to unmeasured quantum baths, Kramer's rule no longer applies due to non-ergodic behavior. Our analysis shows that non-resonant coupling to multiple unobserved baths breaks Kramer's degeneracy, leading to different ground states on both sides of time reversal symmetry, with the two states remaining orthogonal to each other. We also observed that a non-invariant subspace of the reduced system's Liouvillian spectrum can be associated with a non-orthogonal superposition of the two time-reversal symmetric states. Furthermore, our research indicates that the non-orthogonal superposition undergoes periodic changes under time-reversal operations, leading to possible revival of the Kramers degeneracy. We verified our findings using the Heisenberg XXZ model and its quantum-ancilla algorithm representation.

In highly mobile scenarios for massive MIMO systems, which are often encountered in vehicle environments, the channel state information (CSI) feedback faces significant challenges due to rapidly changing wireless signal conditions. Consequently, existing CSI feedback models may become obsolete. To address this problem, we propose a novel data-driven approach based on long short-term memory (LSTM) to predict CSI values for highly mobile MIMO systems by leveraging past observations and incorporating a unique input strategy that utilizes the product of current and prior CSI values. The effectiveness of our method is evaluated and compared with recent solutions using realistic simulations.

Regional economic disparity assessments serve as a vital economic development indicator. This paper develops a small-area estimator for the Elteto-Kovesi inequality index using data from the Hungarian General Census of 2006, focusing on rural areas. Two types of auxiliary information are incorporated into the estimation: regional, aggregated data and individual-level data. We also investigate the efficacy of various regression functions based on auxiliary data. To account for the Elteto-Kovesi index's non-standard distribution, a family of beta-related densities is proposed, allowing for a straightforward derivation of variance estimates. We evaluate the performance of these estimators through Monte Carlo simulations and apply them to real-world data analysis.

In a hermitian complex manifold featuring a non-degenerate self-intersection curve, we establish scaling asymptotics for the Szegö kernel on the curve when the dimension of the holomorphic tangent bundle is odd. By doing so, we derive a representation of near-diagonal Szegö projectors as integrals of the Grauert tube metrics' geodesic curvature, yielding further results including the diagonal Szegö projectors' $L^2$-norms, $L^2$-norms of the Szegö kernel, and a particular formula for the Grauert tube's metric curvature.

The algorithm MARINLINGA is a revised version of Roussopoulos's method for producing a line graph from a given graph. MARINLINGA's primary function lies in its ability to create a complete graph from a given line graph. By employing MARINLINGA, a complete graph can be constructed from a given line graph. This study presents a straightforward approach to implementing MARINLINGA, accompanied by an illustration using an example. Furthermore, this paper validates the efficacy of MARINLINGA through a statistical analysis comparing the performance of the algorithm to Roussopoulos's method. The results of this comparison are also explored in depth.

This paper validates Lee-Lee's hypothesis by demonstrating an equivalence between the roots associated with non-self-intersecting curves in a closed unit disk and their associated associated closed formal flows.

The growing size of software packages with unnecessary features has been a long-standing concern, which in Java programs is exacerbated by the increasing complexity of dependencies. Although previous research has only provided a snapshot view of this issue, this paper uses an extensive dataset of Java projects to explore the dynamics of dependency bloat over time. By examining a large number of projects with multiple daily updates, the results reveal a worrying trend of rapidly growing dependency problems, which in some cases results in significant fluctuations in project size. Notably, the majority of projects experience a steady, consistent growth in unnecessary dependencies, which in a few cases reaches alarming levels. These findings highlight the need for tools to monitor and manage this issue, as well as the potential benefits of using data-driven decision support to help developers identify and remove unnecessary features from their software.

In this study, we utilize entangled biphotons generated from spontaneous parametric down conversion as a source for non-classical states. Four distinct types of entangled biphoton pairs are created, each characterized by a unique statistical distribution $\rho$, based on the relative control the photons exert over a synapse. The types of entangled biphotons are distinguished by their degree of kinship, which reflects the interrelatedness of the photons, measured using the family of Tsallis entropies. Through the controlled synthesis of states, we demonstrate that the types of entangled biphotons are characterized by a non-monotonic relationship between the degree of kinship and control, with a specific region of antagonism where increased control leads to decreased kinship. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entropy of the distribution $\rho$ is distinct from the kinship of the entangled biphotons, which highlights the complexity and uniqueness of the controlled synthesis of states.

This research examines multistage distributionally robust optimization based on a risk measure that combines worst-case scenarios with a distance metric centered on a reference distribution. A new class of scenario constructions is introduced, where effective scenarios are added or removed at each stage to minimize risk according to the specified distance metric. This approach results in a problem formulation that can be solved using a conditional scenario optimization framework. This method offers several benefits, including the ability to refine scenario sets using new information and efficiently compute optimal solutions using a feedback loop. A key challenge is identifying optimal effective scenarios, for which a linearization algorithm is provided to enable the use of standard optimization solvers. A numerical case study illustrates the application of this method, demonstrating its superiority over alternative approaches in a multiproduct, multiperiod supply chain optimization problem.

While researchers have made significant strides in predicting future actions from videos, a major limitation remains in capturing future scene dynamics. To address this, a new method utilizes a Radial Basis Function neural network to learn temporal features and model long-range dependencies in videos. By applying a feature mapping Regularized Recurrent Neural Network, our approach effectively captures complex scene context and object interactions essential for anticipating actions, particularly in situations with unobserved objects. In contrast to previous methods, our approach achieves improved performance, particularly in scenarios involving unobserved objects. Furthermore, our method demonstrates competitive results on the EPIC-KITCHENS, ACTiON, and ACTING-KITCHENS datasets under observed and unobserved object conditions.

In a one-dimensional system consisting of two distinct elements connected by a central mediator, we study the process of thermalization due to interactions with the mediator. This model is examined under scenarios where the system is initially in an isolated state and then coupled to the mediator. Both scenarios are analyzed using linear response theory and result in the formation of equilibrium states at significantly different timescales. These timescales are determined by the system's local properties, with one depending on the system's overall energy and the other on the energy of the specific interaction channel. This model demonstrates how local interactions can lead to distinct design times for thermalization, even when the system reaches equilibrium at the same global time scale.

We investigate pseudo-differential operators on homogeneous trees by drawing inspiration from the Euclidean case to define these operators. We then derive a symbolic representation for them. Subsequently, we find the criteria under which these pseudo-differential operators behave consistently. Lastly, we determine the necessary conditions under which these operators become negligible (nuclear) measurements.

The use of 5G networks has been met with concerns regarding the excessive energy consumption and exposure to RF radiation of 5G smartphones during the initial internet connection process. This study aims to alleviate users' concerns by comparing the energy consumption and exposure levels of smartphones with the latest 5G NR standard against base stations using reduced power output and reduced bandwidth. The research involves developing a new method for estimating energy consumption and RF exposure using a single measurement at the network side, thus eliminating the need for expensive equipment. The findings of this study will be compared to current standards such as 5G NR, 4G LTE, and Wi-Fi. A preliminary assessment using a 5G NR smartphone will also be conducted.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) often exhibit overconfidence in cases where their input data falls outside the training domain. To mitigate this problem, our proposed approach, called an adversarial loss and support (ALAS), involves learning an outlier distribution and utilizing ALAS for training an ensemble model. The ALAS training framework involves learning a conditional data distribution and an outlier distribution, with the latter serving as a data generator. The ALAS loss is derived from the Chamfer distance between these two distributions. During inference, the ALAS framework generates synthetic data outside the training domain using the learned outlier distribution. The ALAS score of a test input serves as a measure of its out-of-distribution confidence, thereby preventing overconfidence. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of ALAS in preventing overconfidence and ensuring robustness against out-of-distribution inputs.

This study examines the angular patterns of jet formations in high-energy proton-proton collisions at a 13 TeV collision speed using data collected by CMS. The research investigates the relationships between jet angles in events containing two, three, or four jets and assesses how these patterns vary based on the jet's transverse momentum and the number of participating particles. The data's theoretical background is matched with predictions from event generators, which also evaluate potential effects from the presence of multiple parton emissions and heavy-flavor interactions.

Deep learning models have demonstrated exceptional performance in computer vision tasks, primarily through supervised training. However, relying on extensive labelled data for training has proven both expensive and time-consuming. To mitigate these issues, research has been focused on developing efficient, semi-supervised, and unsupervised deep learning approaches that require minimal labelled data for initial training and none at all. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the state-of-the-art deep learning methods employed in semi-supervised and unsupervised learning environments for visual tasks. The survey is divided into five key sections that cover semi-supervised learning techniques based on the type of data augmentation used, the type of models employed, the approach to loss calculation, the use of adversarial learning, and the incorporation of generative models. It also examines recent advancements in the field and offers guidance on future research directions.

Detecting anomalies in datasets has long been a critical challenge across various fields, with one specific task being the identification of anomalies based on how well they fit established models. A new method, RECol, tackles this task by leveraging the differences in error between normal data points and outliers. RECol does this by training models on normal data and then applying these models to the entire dataset, which results in error values for each data point. Anomaly detection is then performed by identifying data points with error values that fall significantly below their median or mean. Notably, RECol can identify anomalies in both numerical and categorical data, and it has been shown to be effective even when there are no normal data points to train on. Instead, users can add artificial data to the training set. Evaluations of RECol on synthetic and real-world datasets have shown it to perform better than state-of-the-art methods in most cases.

This paper formulates a novel class of regularity criteria for a broad class of Young-type equations, encompassing diverse orders of nonlinearity that are initially assumed to exhibit a level of Lipschitz continuity with certain elliptical and exponential constraints. Through a detailed analysis, we identify the optimal criteria for specific scenarios, and through a series of iterative modifications, establish the optimal $L^p$-regularity criteria for Young-type equations with nonlinearity of all orders. Furthermore, a specific non-linear elliptic equation is analyzed to demonstrate the utility of our results.

The standard model weakly interacts with light, and as a result, it predicts that neutrinos have an extremely small magnetic moment, which in turn would result in neutrino- photon interactions. However, when it comes to neutrino interactions with extremely strong magnetic fields found in magnetars, the magnetic moment's suppression due to its mass is significantly reduced, and as a result, the interaction may become more prominent.  The interaction of neutrinos with extremely strong magnetic fields could be a potential explanation for the possible discrepancy in the gravitational wave data from the event GW190814, which may suggest that the mass of the lighter component could be as low as 2.5 to 10 Solar masses.  The interaction of neutrinos with extremely strong magnetic fields also opens up a potential area of research in the neutrino sector, which could be explored through the observation of the timing and spectral properties of the X-ray flares from the event GW190814.

In recent years, researchers have made significant progress in uncovering the dynamics of glial cells and identifying their crucial role in brain disorders. Emerging evidence suggests glial cells form synapses with neurons, which has led to the development of theoretical models. This study builds on a previous mean field model by incorporating a more realistic representation of glial cell synapses and neuronal activity. Our findings reveal that this revised model gives rise to stable limit cycles, with altered parameters causing transitions between different limit cycle periods. Notably, the model exhibits a transition from simple oscillations to complex multistability, and we identify a parameter range where complex oscillations are favored. The results suggest that glial cells and their network structure are crucial for generating rhythmic activity in the brain, and for maintaining normal brain function.

This study focuses on a theoretical model of a neutral spin-1/2 particle moving within an inhomogeneous magnetic field, specifically in a neutral Yeshivasahai field. We investigate the topological characteristics of this system by calculating the Berry phase, focusing on two one-dimensional subspaces - one where the magnetic field is constant, associated with an Abelian topological structure, and one where the system behaves like a multi-level system, characterized by an non-Abelian topological behavior.

The impact of first-passages in random walks on boundary recession in confined systems is a fundamental problem in physics, which has been examined using a model of alternating motion. The research reveals a crucial role of competition between diffusion and first-passage properties in determining how boundaries shrink in response to random walks of varying intensity. A fundamental threshold is identified, below which boundaries grow consistently, and another is identified, above which boundaries grow erratically. The findings provide insights into the fundamental principles governing boundary recession, complementing established rules in this area. The specific characteristics of one-dimensional systems with alternating motion are also explored.

For a knot K, we establish a relationship between the hyperbolic volume of K and the coefficients of the F-spectral series of the knot's complement M_K, where M_K's signature is (g,1). We then derive upper limits for the hyperbolic volume of (g,1) knots, with g being odd, to be of O(g^-2). This outcome arises from proving that there exists a family of hyperbolic L-space knots, with g being odd, and their formal semigroups consisting of cubes, resulting in M_K's signature growth rate of O(g).

A kinetic theory for a gas is represented by a countable number of particles, 
each represented by a variable (position, momentum) within a specific probability space. 
This space is comprised of two separate components - the space of infinite-dimensional positions and the space of infinite-dimensional momentums. 
This paper introduces a poisson map from the space of particles to the space of states, 
which preserves the order of values, as well as a corresponding map from the space of states to the space of hydrodynamic variables. 
This paper also examines the properties of these maps, including their relationship to the H-theorem, 
hence providing a general framework for a kinetic theory, such as the Boltzmann equation, 
which accounts for non-constant entropy in the space of particles.

In our proposed contribution, we suggest a novel approach to enhance the reliability of models developed for detecting artifacts in endoscopic video frames. By leveraging the capabilities of an ensemble of object detection models trained on the same dataset, we aim to overcome the limitations of individual models. Our proposed framework, Ensemble of Models (EoM), is designed to produce more robust results by mitigating the sensitivity of single models to variations in video frame quality, such as changes in illumination, texture, and motion caused by the insertion of the endoscope. To evaluate the effectiveness of EoM, we conducted a comparative study of the performance of models trained on the M-Endoscopy Dataset, using the most advanced object detection models. Our analysis included a comparison of the predictive accuracy of individual models and EoM, with the latter demonstrating superior results. Our study also involved a comparative evaluation of the predictive accuracy and predictive exclusivity of both individual models and EoM, with the aim of assessing the potential of EoM for reducing false positives in various clinical settings. Our proposed framework, EoM, is expected to provide valuable insights into the feasibility of using ensemble models in medical image analysis, with a focus on improving the robustness of models developed for detecting artifacts in endoscopic video frames.

Code written by humans tends to exhibit certain patterns and tendencies that are often overlooked by machines. This inherent structure, referred to as grammatical patterns, can be uncovered and analyzed using formal grammar techniques, such as context-free grammars, to extract meaningful insights. This study delves into the investigation of grammatical patterns within the names of code elements, such as classes, functions, variables, and other components. By establishing a general framework for defining these patterns, the research explores the potential semantics and context behind their creation. To this end, three distinct grammatical patterns relevant to object-oriented programming are defined and applied to real-world software. The analysis yields a comprehensive understanding of how these patterns evolve over time, including how their characteristics are influenced by factors like time, programming styles, and developer populations. Additionally, the research demonstrates how these discovered patterns can be leveraged to generate informative and helpful code comments.

We create a module for the operator $\Box_q$ using the $q$-shuffle algebra associated with the affine Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, and in the process, we resolve several issues previously encountered by other researchers. These include determining the bases for the operator $\Box_q$, establishing the operator $\Box_q$-module isomorphism, and finding a combinatorial method to calculate the values of certain functions associated with the operator $\Box_q$.

The formation of polycrystalline microstructures through grain growth is a crucial factor in determining the properties of engineering materials with complex microstructures, such as duplex and triplex steels. Understanding the dynamic interactions between grains during this process is essential for accurately predicting their final microstructure. This study develops a computational model to simulate grain-growth dynamics in multi-grain systems by integrating a grain-growth law with a probabilistic algorithm. The model is based on experimental data from ref. 1 and its performance is validated through comparison with actual grain configurations. Furthermore, our results indicate that the presence of third grains significantly accelerates grain-boundary migration in dual-grain systems, and the model is capable of replicating the diverse interactions observed in complex grain arrangements, including grain coalescence, dissolution, and boundary curvature changes.

The literature on 3D human pose and shape estimation has largely centered on comparing different algorithms. However, despite the vast array of methods proposed, little has been done to explore the influence of diverse training conditions on model performance. This study investigates the impact of various training-related factors on pose and shape estimation tasks, including dataset quality, multi-task learning, data quantity, subject diversity, and label accuracy. To this end, we introduce the Human3D benchmark, a comprehensive framework for evaluating 3D human recovery methods. The benchmark offers advanced tools for generating synthetic datasets and assessing performance across 13 benchmark methods, uncovering notable trends and insights along the way. The project and benchmark are accessible at http://human3d.bijan111.com.

In a diluted system of negative U-centers, where strong electron-electron repulsion exists, we examine the conditions necessary for superconductivity to occur. For this analysis, we simplify the attractive electron interaction into two distinct components: a short-range attractive force that facilitates pairing and a long-range Coulomb repulsion. We demonstrate that below a critical attraction threshold, a d-wave pairing symmetry emerges, characterized by a transition temperature that is proportional to the square of the attraction parameter when the interatomic distance is much greater than the size of the Cooper pair. Furthermore, we highlight the potential applications of superconductivity with a large gap in the molecular bovine band and suggest that this approach may lead to the discovery of novel superconducting materials with enhanced critical temperature and magnetic properties.

We present a comprehensive model based on scalar leptoquarks that accounts for their interactions with all Standard Model fermions and bosons, enabling it to efficiently compute higher-order corrections and cross-sections using FeynRules. This leptoquark model is defined by two SU(2)_L triplets, with each component denoted as \tilde{q}_{1} and \tilde{q}_{2}, which are further characterised by three distinct isospin values: Q_{1,2}^{1,2} and Q_{1,2}^{3}. By default, both leptoquarks are assumed to be equivalent in terms of their isospin components. This leptoquirk model seamlessly integrates into the MadGraph framework, allowing users to easily expand its capabilities and extend its scope to include any other beyond Standard Model particles. This comprehensive model is available for download through the INSPIRE dataset repository, labelled as EX1709.

Machine learning has become a widely applied science, generating diverse concepts drawn from disparate fields like algebra, topology, and statistical mechanics. Although the connections between these ideas and mathematical disciplines are becoming more prominent, the underlying links between them remain obscure. This survey aims to provide insight into these connections by establishing a link between the concepts in machine learning and the language of category theory. By doing so, it offers an organized framework within which machine learning can be studied in a more theoretical and coherent manner.

A new terminal sliding-mode control approach is introduced to enhance the precision and efficiency of conventional TSM techniques. In this approach, a non-integer order is applied to the sliding surface, resulting in N/2, where N represents the total degree of the system's dynamics. By doing so, this strategy attains superior performance compared to traditional TSM methods. Furthermore, this approach has potential advantages in terms of robustness against disturbances and chatter. Furthermore, this strategy has potential advantages in terms of robustness against disturbances and chatter.

Lithium-ion batteries are becoming increasingly crucial for the UK's energy future, yet their performance in both quality and quantity is difficult to measure due to the lack of suitable, non-destructive techniques. We've developed a method to assess the internal chemistry of LIBs using ultrasonic testing on Prismatic and Pouch cell types. By applying an acoustic force to the cell and analyzing the resulting echoes, we've discovered that different dimensions create distinct patterns that can be detected and measured. Our findings show that the layering within the cell influences how the ultrasonic waves vibrate within the liquid electrolyte, allowing us to create detailed images of the cell's internal layout. By using precise mathematical equations and testing our results against realistic and hypothetical scenarios, we've confirmed the accuracy of our results. Our research demonstrates the potential for ultrasonic testing as a reliable, non-invasive way to examine the internal structure of lithium-ion batteries.

This study focuses on designing a discrete-time tracking control system for a gantry crane using flatness-based methods. The system's dynamics are first modeled using discrete-time equations, taking into account sampling time, and the Derivative Operator Approach is used to eliminate derivatives of the system's states. A linear controller is then proposed, which achieves flatness-based tracking within a specified time horizon, and the study also addresses issues related to input saturation, dynamic feedback, and digital implementation. The feasibility of the controller is demonstrated through a simulation using a real-world crane system.

Collecting large-scale data for image captioning is an inexact process prone to errors of both quality and relevance. The presence of these errors leads to noisy data, which negatively affects the performance of machine translation models during training. In our research, we focus on a novel approach known as cooperative distillation to address this issue and aim to distinguish clean captions from noisy captions within the training dataset. By doing so, we can ensure that the captions used to update the model, whether through forward passes or backpropagation, come from high-quality sources. Our proposed method is tested on the MSCOCO dataset, where we artificially introduced various levels of noise into the training data, and the results demonstrate a significant improvement in captioning performance, with a notable gain of 1.0 points in BLEU-1 scores over traditional models that do not use cooperative distillation.

We define well-connected strings within the product set $[n_1] \times... \times [n_d]$ as subsets whose projected images onto each subsequence of indices $[1, k]$ contain at most one element. Our work generalizes previous research on well-connected subsets of binary strings by Knauer and Ruscenda to a more comprehensive model. The current investigation also builds upon and enhances the query-based framework for well-connected sets of strings initially proposed by Gal and Stav.

Ehresmann semigroups extend group-like structures with a multiplicative and associative binary operation that incorporates a partial order, allowing elements to be compared in two separate contexts. This extension is notable for its inclusion of a wide variety of mathematical structures such as ordered groups, lattice groups, hypergroups, and star-averaged groups within a unified framework. The primary objective of this comprehensive study is to provide a thorough and definitive analysis of Ehresmann semigroups, focusing on their inherent properties and those of their subcategories. The paper serves as a substantial and up-to-date reference on Ehresmann semigroups and their associated categories, with detailed discussions on fundamental concepts, examples, and applications. This research paper is divided into sections that cover category properties, ordered structures, specific types of Ehresmann semigroups, and their interconnections, culminating in a discussion on representations and categorical relationships.

Recent self-attention studies have shown it to be an effective feature for achieving state-of-the-art results in natural language processing and other tasks.  However, its theoretical properties are not fully understood.  We've developed a theoretical framework to analyze the self-attention mechanism in linear models and its interaction with the depth-to-width interplay.
